resources.title: Bash Backup Script Template
resources.description: Portable backup script with rotation, logging, and dry-run mode.
resources.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Simple backup with dry-run and rotation
set -euo pipefail
SRC="${1:-$HOME/Documents}"
DEST="${2:-$HOME/backups}"
DRY_RUN="${DRY_RUN:-0}"
STAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)
TARGET="$DEST/backup-$STAMP"

mkdir -p "$DEST"
if [[ "$DRY_RUN" == "1" ]]; then
  echo "[dry-run] Would copy $SRC -> $TARGET"
  exit 0
fi

mkdir -p "$TARGET"
cp -a "$SRC" "$TARGET/"
echo "Backup complete: $TARGET"

# Keep last 7 backups
ls -1dt "$DEST"/backup-* 2>/dev/null | tail -n +8 | xargs -r rm -rf

resources.title: Safe Local Port Check Script
resources.description: Check listening ports on your own machine (not for unauthorized scanning).
resources.body:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# List listening TCP ports on this machine
if command -v ss >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  ss -tuln
elif command -v netstat >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  netstat -tuln
else
  echo "Install ss or netstat"
  exit 1
fi

resources.title: Network Topology Types (Star, Mesh, Hybrid)
resources.description: Visual overview of common topologies with when to use each — interview and Network+ ready.
resources.body:
NETWORK TOPOLOGY TYPES (quick guide)

1) STAR
   Devices connect to a central switch.
   + Easy to manage  - Switch is critical

        PC -- Switch -- PC
                 |
                PC

2) EXTENDED STAR
   Multiple access switches under a core/distribution switch.
   Used in real buildings and campuses.

3) MESH (full or partial)
   Multiple paths between nodes for resilience.
   + Redundancy  - Cost/complexity

4) HYBRID
   What enterprises actually run: star access + hierarchical core + edge firewall.

5) BUS / RING
   Mostly exam history for modern Ethernet LANs.
   Know definitions; design with star + hierarchy.

INTERVIEW ONE-LINER
"Access layers are usually star; the campus is hierarchical; the WAN may use partial mesh."

resources.title: 3-Tier Campus Architecture Explained
resources.description: Core, distribution, and access layers — plus when to use a collapsed core.
resources.body:
3-TIER CAMPUS MODEL

ACCESS
- End devices: PCs, phones, APs, printers
- Port security, PoE, VLAN assignment

DISTRIBUTION
- Policy, routing between VLANs, aggregation
- ACLs, summarization (as design allows)

CORE
- High-speed backbone, keep it simple and fast
- Connect distribution blocks

COLLAPSED CORE (2-TIER)
- Merge core + distribution for smaller networks
- Cheaper, fewer devices, still valid design

ASCII SKETCH
        [CORE]
       /  |  \
   [DIST][DIST][DIST]
     |     |     |
   access access access

Talk about failure domains: one access switch down shouldn't take the whole campus.

resources.title: DMZ & Perimeter Sketch
resources.description: Simple perimeter diagram: Internet, firewall, LAN, and DMZ for public services.
resources.body:
DMZ / PERIMETER (starter sketch)

                 Internet
                     |
              [Edge Firewall]
               /          \
           [LAN]          [DMZ]
        users/apps     web / mail / VPN portal
                            |
                     (optional internal FW)
                            |
                      sensitive systems

RULES OF THUMB
- Don't put public web servers flat on the staff LAN
- Limit DMZ → LAN to only required ports
- Log denials and critical allows
- Prefer reverse proxy / WAF patterns when possible

HOME LAB TOPOLOGY (starter)

[Internet / ISP]

[Home Router]  (NAT)

- What each VM is for (AD, DNS, web, etc.)

resources.title: VLAN Basics for Diagrams
resources.description: How to show VLANs, trunks, and access ports on a whiteboard without panic.
resources.body:
VLANS ON A DIAGRAM

ACCESS PORT = one VLAN to a PC/phone
TRUNK = multiple VLANs between switches (802.1Q tags)

Sketch:
[PC VLAN10]--access--[SW1]==trunk==[SW2]--access--[PC VLAN20]

If VLANs differ, they need a router/L3/firewall to talk (inter-VLAN routing).

DRAWING TIP
Color-code or label each link: "access 10" vs "trunk 10,20,30".

resources.title: Topology Symbol Cheatsheet
resources.description: Common shapes and labels used on network diagrams (cloud, firewall, switch, server).
resources.body:
DIAGRAM SYMBOL CHEATSHEET

Cloud        = Internet / ISP / MPLS
Rectangle    = Router or L3 device
Switch icon  = L2/L3 switch
Cylinder     = Server / database
Phone/laptop = End users
Dashed box   = Security zone (DMZ, guest, PCI)
Firewall     = Filter / policy point (label INSIDE/OUTSIDE/DMZ)

ALWAYS LABEL
- Device role
- VLAN or subnet
- Trust boundary
- North arrow optional; top=Internet is fine
